fields.description:
## Why

Every plan-review criterion that mentions the two headings POOLS them and applies ONE bar —
F1 reads "each acceptance/success criterion", G3 "each parent acceptance/success criterion",
G7 fetches "What/Scope/Success Criteria/Acceptance Criteria" as one contract. The dual
vocabulary is therefore noise in the rubrics: it suggests to the reviewing model a distinction
the criteria do not implement, and it is the source the generated criteria guide is built from.
This story removes it at the source.

## What

Rename Success Criteria -> Acceptance Criteria throughout the reviewer prompts and the criteria
routing index, then REGENERATE the criteria guide from them.

## Scope

Reviewer prompts (`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`):
- `plan_review_F1.md:10` — "each acceptance/success criterion" -> "each acceptance criterion"
- `plan_review_G3.md:10` and `:12` — line 12 carries BOTH bare-`SC` tokens in the repo:
  "THREE SC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS" and "'SC says zero matches, the DD annotates exceptions'"
- `plan_review_G5.md:19` ("a set of unrelated success criteria" — the decomposition tell,
  which DOES mean the ticket's criteria), `plan_review_G7.md:12` and `:16`,
  `plan_review_COH.md:10`, `plan_review_container.md:14`
- `completion_verifier.md:59` — the Epic bullet naming `## Success Criteria`

Routing index `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — the `check` strings at
`:544` (COH), `:830` (G3), `:908` (G7).

Regenerate `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` with
`python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` — it is GENERATED and
carries a do-not-hand-edit banner; all 11 of its SC hits are downstream of the files above.

EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED — `plan_review_T2.md:10`. Its phrase is "a pilot with success metrics ...
or stated success criteria for a trial": generic English for the metrics that define whether an
EXPERIMENT succeeded, not the ticket heading. Renaming it to "acceptance criteria for a trial"
would change T2's meaning. This is the same false-positive class as `O-RAN-SC`; the site is
recorded here so a later sweep does not "fix" it.

OUT OF SCOPE: the `dod_uncertifiable` / "definition-of-done" wording in
`plan_review_verifier.md:81`, `plan_review_verifier_agentic.md:87` and
`review_kernel/verify_models.py:231` — a related but distinct concept, tracked separately.

## Approach

Textual substitution in the listed files only. Two forms appear and both are handled:
the phrase "acceptance/success criteria|criterion" collapses to "acceptance criteria|criterion"
(not "acceptance/acceptance"), and standalone "Success Criteria" becomes "Acceptance Criteria".
G3's two bare-`SC` tokens are edited by hand, not by pattern, because `\bSC\b` also matches
`O-RAN-SC` elsewhere in the repo. Their exact replacements are:
`THREE SC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS` -> `THREE AC-CONTRADICTION PATTERNS`, and
`'SC says zero matches, the DD annotates exceptions'` ->
`'the AC says zero matches, the DD annotates exceptions'`.

Editing `criteria_routing.json` rotates the `regver` criteria-registry stamp, which on TODAY's
`main` invalidates every outstanding plan-review attestation (632 tickets, ~40
open/in_progress) as `stale-regver`. Ticket `1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` (ADR 0053) grandfathers that
at the claim gate, and it HAS now merged — Gerrit change 962 landed as `095c4afef` and the
ticket is closed. This story's `depends_on 1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` was a genuine MERGE-ORDER
constraint, not a preference: landing this rename first would have stranded ~40 in-flight
claims behind a full LLM re-review. That prerequisite is now SATISFIED, so the routing edit
is safe to make. (Status refreshed during implementation; the plan previously recorded 962
as still awaiting its votes.)

Once grandfathering has landed, the rotation is harmless at the claim gate (attestations stay
valid and report non-blocking `registry_drift`). It DOES still deny progressive drift-refresh
reuse, which is correct and expected.

## Testing

- Regenerate the guide and assert it is free of SC vocabulary (the regeneration is itself the
  check that the generator was run rather than the file hand-edited).
- `pytest tests/unit -k "criteria or routing or registry"` green.
- A test that captures `registry_version(None)` BEFORE applying the routing edit (from the
  pre-edit file content) and asserts it differs afterwards, so the rotation is proven by
  construction rather than compared against a literal that would rot the moment any other
  change touches `criteria_routing.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rniE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` returns no matches.
- [ ] `grep -noE "\bSCs?\b" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G3.md` returns no matches (both
      bare tokens renamed).
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is regenerated by the documented command, still
      carries its GENERATED banner, and `grep -niE "success[ _-]criteri(a|on)"` on it is empty.
- [ ] Verified BEFORE the routing edit is made: `rebar.llm.plan_review.attest.compute_validity`
      no longer returns a blocking `stale-regver` verdict on the branch point (i.e. ticket
      `1f32-f86e-8a51-4d8e` has merged), asserted by a check against the current checkout rather
      than assumed.
- [ ] A test proves `registry_version(None)` computed from the PRE-edit routing content differs
      from `registry_version(None)` computed after the edit — capturing both values at run time,
      asserting inequality, and hard-coding neither.
- [ ] `grep -n "success criteria" src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T2.md` still returns its
      one match, proving the deliberately excluded pilot-metrics phrase was left intact.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the full pytest suite pass.
